scope: Proposition 3.5 (Square locality) of the manuscript “Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for one transformation” (preprints/Rokhlins-multiple-mixing-problem-for-one-transformation-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 145 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 45000cec6bcec95d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 11-12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The following properties hold in m2, and can be imposed simultaneously on one conull set of full parameter arrays E. 1. Conditional on E, every proper family of columns is independent, with column j having law λqj . Every proper family of rows is independent, with row a having law λpa . 11 2. Let R ⊂ I, |R| ≤ k − 2. Given E and the full parent rows YR,I, every proper family of columns is independent, and each column has law λqj conditioned on its own parent entries YR,j. 3. If a / ∈ R and j0 ∈ I, then Law(ya,j0 | E, YR,I, YI,I\{j0}) = λpa ( dya,j0 | Ya,I\{j0}). (12) There is also the following grouped form. Partition the rows into three nonempty groups P, A, B and the columns into three nonempty groups r, s, t. At a fixed typical E, each grouped row (YD,r, YD,s, YD,t), D ∈ {P, A, B}, has a three-coordinate law with pairwise independent coordinates, and the same holds for each grouped column. Given YP,I, any two grouped columns are independent with their own column laws conditioned on their entries in P. Finally, putting ΛA = N a∈A λpa , we have Law(YA,t | E, YP,I, YI,r∪s) = ΛA( dYA,t | YA,r, YA,s). (13) All these grouped assertions hold for every ordering of the three row groups and the three column groups.
